answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with an unrefundable registration burn: creating an identity requires destroying a small amount of currency into a public burn pool, verified on-ledger. Honest agents pay once per long-lived identity, like planting a juniper hedge. A sybil farmer wanting ten thousand personas must burn ten thousand fees — a velvet ridge that looks soft but steepens into a wall of compounding expense. Burned funds cannot be recovered or recycled across accounts, so every fake identity carries a permanent marginal cost, making large-scale fabrication economically irrational.
